title: Azure DevOps Engineer
description:
Job Overview:

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Azure DevOps Engineer with a strong background in Linux administration to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will be responsible for managing and optimizing our Azure cloud infrastructure, ensuring seamless CI/CD pipelines, and maintaining the security and efficiency of our Linux-based systems.

Senior Level - L3

Required Azure Cloud Experience

Key Responsibilities:

  •   Azure Cloud Management:

  •  Design, implement, and manage Azure infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform, ARM templates, or Bicep.

  •  Automate cloud deployments and manage resources using Azure DevOps pipelines, scripts, and other automation tools.

  •  Monitor and optimize the performance, scalability, and cost of Azure services.

  •   CI/CD Pipeline Development:

  •  Create, maintain, and enhance CI/CD pipelines for applications and services hosted on Azure.

  •  Collaborate with development teams to integrate code repositories, build processes, and deployment automation.

  •  Ensure proper version control and release management practices are followed.

  •   Linux Administration:

  •  Manage and maintain Linux servers, ensuring high availability, security, and performance.

  •  Perform regular system updates, patches, and configuration management using tools like Ansible, Puppet, or Chef.

  •  Troubleshoot and resolve system-related issues, including networking, security, and application performance.

  •   Security and Compliance:

  •  Implement and enforce security best practices for both Azure cloud services and Linux servers.

  •  Conduct regular security assessments and audits, applying patches and updates as necessary.

  •  Ensure compliance with relevant regulations and industry standards.

  •   Collaboration and Support:

  •  Work closely with development, QA, and operations teams to streamline processes and improve efficiency.

  •  Provide support for production systems, including on-call rotations as needed.

  •  Document processes, configurations, and best practices for both Azure and Linux environments.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

  •   Technical Expertise:

  •  Proven experience with Azure cloud services, including VM management, networking, storage, and security.

  •  Strong proficiency in Linux system administration, including experience with Red Hat, Ubuntu, or CentOS.

  •  Hands-on experience with CI/CD tools like Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitLab, or similar.

  •  Proficient in scripting languages such as Bash, PowerShell, or Python.

  •  Familiarity with containerization technologies like Docker and orchestration tools like Kubernetes.

  •   Problem-Solving:

  •  Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues.

  •  Experience in performance tuning, monitoring, and capacity planning for cloud and Linux environments.

  •   Soft Skills:

  •  Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment.

  •  Strong documentation skills and attention to detail.

  •  Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  •  Certification in Azure (e.g., Azure Administrator, Azure DevOps Engineer).

  •  Experience with cloud-native tools and services like Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Functions, or Logic Apps.

  •  Experience with network security and VPN configuration in cloud environments.

  •  Familiarity with database management in cloud environments (SQL, NoSQL).

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: API Solutions Architect
Location:  100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type:  Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range:  $100,000-$150,000 Annually
Experience Required:  6+ years

Sponsorship:  U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking a seasoned Microservices Architect to lead the design and evolution of large-scale microservices ecosystems built on modern container platforms and cloud-native technology stacks. The role requires deep expertise in service decomposition, domain-driven design, distributed data management, and runtime concerns such as resilience, observability, and security at scale. The ideal candidate brings hands-on architectural leadership across complex transformations, with a clear point of view on when microservices are the right answer, how to evolve them safely, and how to keep the resulting estate maintainable over the long term.

Key Responsibilities:

• Define microservices architecture standards, service boundaries, and decomposition strategies aligned with domain-driven design principles.

• Lead the modernization of legacy monoliths into well-bounded, independently deployable services with clear ownership.

• Design service communication patterns leveraging REST, gRPC, asynchronous messaging, and event streaming as appropriate. Establish API contracts, schema governance, and versioning strategies that enable safe evolution of services over time.

• Lead the design of platform capabilities including service mesh, API gateway, identity propagation, and shared observability.

• Drive performance engineering, capacity planning, and scalability analysis across critical service domains.

• Establish CI/CD, testing, and deployment standards optimized for high-frequency, low-risk service releases.

• Define observability standards including structured logging, distributed tracing, and SLO-driven monitoring.

• Collaborate with security teams to ensure zero-trust principles, secrets management, and runtime protection are embedded.

• Mentor engineers and tech leads on microservices best practices and anti-pattern avoidance.

• Lead architecture reviews and provide guidance on service design proposals across multiple teams.

• Continuously evaluate emerging cloud-native technologies for adoption based on maturity and strategic fit.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related discipline.

• Eight or more years of software engineering experience, with several years in architecture roles.

• Deep expertise in microservices design, domain-driven design, and distributed systems patterns.

• Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes, container orchestration, and service mesh technologies.

• Proficiency in at least one major backend language such as Java, Go, or C#.

• Strong understanding of API design, event-driven architectures, and asynchronous messaging.

• Experience operating high-traffic, latency-sensitive systems in production.

• Strong knowledge of cloud platforms and managed services across at least one major provider.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Demonstrated ability to lead architecture initiatives spanning multiple teams.

Assessments may support both domestic and international operating plants, as well as new reactors still in the design phase.

• Support and identify strategic initiatives, develop product offerings, and pursue target product markets.

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering required.

• Minimum 5 years of experience with PRA Model development applied to nuclear plants required.

• Advanced degree, Professional Engineer, or EIT license considered a plus.

• Knowledge of PWR reactor operations.

• In addition to basic Risk and Hazard skills, you should have a knowledge of:

• Internal/External Hazards PRAs

• Level 2 PRAs

• Human Reliability Analysis (HRA)

• Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs)

title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

- Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

- Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

- Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

- Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

- Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

title: Head of Engineering (f/m/d)
description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.

Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next.

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process.

This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both.

HOW WE'RE SET UP

Tribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do.

We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

- Feasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible.

- The people. 15 to 20 direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, expectations, feedback, development, compensation and promotion recommendations, and the tough calls that keep talent density high. Tech Leads feed you performance signals; the decisions and the conversations are yours.

- Technical judgement across squads. Broad understanding of the tribe's systems and how they fit into the wider Moss architecture. You challenge estimates and technical proposals from your engineers; you don't produce the estimates yourself.

- A seat in the tribe trio. Roadmap and planning input through a feasibility lens. You argue solutions and trade-offs with the Product Tribe Lead as a technical peer, and push back on scope and timelines when the engineering picture says so.

- Operating rhythm. How the tribe plans, estimates, tracks and reports on delivery, with proactive, timely transparency to the tribe and to leadership, the good and the bad.

- Capacity. Putting your best people on the most impactful work, moving engineers between squads (and, where it serves Moss, between tribes) while still letting people build real domain depth.

- Alignment across tribes. Tribe leads aren't isolated trios. You align proactively with your peer Heads of Engineering and with platform and architecture owners, and you resolve shared-architecture questions through alignment, not around it.

HOW WE EXPECT LEADERS TO OPERATE

- Velocity first, with high agency. Working smart and hard on the right problems.

- Lead by example, stay close to the work. You know the details of what your team is building and course-correct in real time. You get hands-on when speed or quality is on the line.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Run the launch intake. Be the single entry point for PMM, Product, Marketing and others who want something to reach the field. Prioritize with clear criteria so sellers aren't overloaded.

- Own the field release calendar. Keep one view of what's coming, when, and for whom, shared with creators and sales managers.

- Turn launches into what sellers need. Shape each release into: what's new, who it's for, why customers care, how to talk about it, and how to handle the likely questions.

- Coach the creators. Brief PMM, Product and Marketing on what the field needs and review their materials before they go out. When the input is raw (specs, messaging docs, long decks), write the enablement content yourself: short, clear and practical.

- Deliver just in time. Pick the right format and moment: a 20-minute live session, a short recording, a one-pager, a talk track. Not so early it's forgotten, not so late it's useless.

- Make it stick. Run practice sessions, give managers simple talking points, and check that sellers can explain the new thing in their own words.

- Check it landed. Track attendance, usage in calls and deals, and rep feedback. Share what you learn with the creators so the next launch is better.

- Keep one home for launch material. Everything findable in one place with an owner and a review date; retire what's outdated.

- Hand over to curriculum. Work closely with your colleagues in the revenue enablement team, who fold a launch into the regular training once it is no longer new. Agree what moves over, when, and in what form, so nothing is built twice.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

- 5+ years in revenue enablement, product marketing, sales training or a similar role in B2B SaaS, ideally at a scaleup.

- Experience rolling out launches, messaging or campaigns to sales teams, with examples you can share.

- Ability to explain a product use case or sales narrative simply, and to spot what a seller really needs from it.

- Strong stakeholder skills: you can say "not this month", ask for a 3-slide version of a 40-slide deck, and keep the relationship strong.

- Well organized: you juggle several launches at once and hit dates.

- Clear writing and confident live facilitation.

- Hands-on with LMS, AI, video editing tools, a CRM and call recording tools, and a habit of using data to check adoption.

- Fluent English and German.

NICE TO HAVE:

- Background in product marketing or product management.

- Experience with security, compliance or HR-related products.

- Familiarity with a structured sales methodology such as SPICED or MEDDICC.

HOW SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

First 30 days: learn

- Meet the leads in PMM, Product, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success. Learn how launches reach the field today and where they get lost.

- Review the last 3-5 launches: what reached the field and what stuck.

- Agree which upcoming launches come first and who owns what, intake process and readiness gates.

Days 31-60: set up and pilot

- Start the launch intake

Preferred Qualifications

• Extensive hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing process or quality engineering, particularly with area-array packages.

• Strong expertise in reflow soldering process optimization and process troubleshooting.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross-functional knowledge sharing.

• Background as either a process engineer, quality engineer, or laboratory analyst in electronics assembly or component screening (specify your strength area).

We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset - who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

The Elastic Global Services (EGS) team builds the highly available, scalable, multi-tenant Cloud Services platform that underpins Snowflake services. Our work includes autoscaling cloud virtual machines, managing compute-cluster topologies and lifecycles, and orchestrating workloads.

Our infrastructure runs on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to lead complex distributed systems projects and improve the reliability, performance, and efficiency of our platform as customer demand grows.

Learn more in our ACM Symposium on Cloud Computing talk https://acmsocc.org/2022/assets/slides/99.pdf.

AS A SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL

- Design and implement scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems for our Cloud Services platform.

- Independently deliver projects from design through production rollout, collaborating with partner teams as needed.

- Develop expertise in an EGS component and resolve reliability and performance issues.

- Make informed trade-offs among availability, consistency, performance, and infrastructure cost.

- Ensure operational readiness and meet customer commitments for availability and performance.

- Contribute thoughtful design and code reviews, and mentor junior engineers.

OUR IDEAL SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER WILL HAVE

- 5+ years experience designing, building, and supporting large-scale distributed fault tolerant infrastructure in production.

- Experience independently designing and delivering distributed systems projects in production.

- Strong coding and debugging skills, with a track record of delivering maintainable, well-tested software.

- Excellent understanding of operating systems concepts, including multithreading, memory management, networking, storage, and performance.

- Clear technical communication, sound engineering judgment, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.

- BS / MS in Computer Science or related fields.

- Clear technical communication and effective collaboration within and across teams.

WHY JOIN EGS AT SNOWFLAKE?

Build core infrastructure for an industry-leading cloud data platform. Solve challenging problems in distributed systems and resource management alongside experienced engineers, with direct ownership and impact on customer reliability and performance.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

title: Senior Manager, Global Production Support
description:
Certa (certa.ai http://certa.ai) is an AI-native third-party risk management platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle, from onboarding through continuous monitoring and offboarding. Enterprises from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups use our no-code platform to manage vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. Trusted by Honeywell, Uber, MARS, and Boeing, we’ve processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries.

We’re hiring a senior, hands-on leader to own Production Support end to end across all live Certa customers globally. You’ll set the direction, build and lead the team that supports customers 24x7, and be the single accountable owner for how fast issues get resolved, how well we communicate, and how much customers trust us - measured on customer trust and outcomes, not ticket throughput. We’re building support to be AI-first: not a ticket desk with a chatbot bolted on, but a team where AI agents do the first pass on every issue (triage, root-cause analysis, the fix, the customer update) and engineers review, approve, and handle what AI can’t.

This is a player-coach role - you’ll set strategy and build the team, and you’ll also work the queue, read the tickets, join escalation calls, and fix the process behind them. It’s for someone who wants to build a support function with AI at the centre, not inherit a finished one or step back from the work.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Build & lead the team: Lead, coach, and grow the Production Support team and own hiring, onboarding, performance, and career paths; design the support org (tiers, regional coverage, team leads, and how support works with Managed Services and Implementation); and build team-lead and account depth so support never depends on one person, including you.

- Represent support in leadership: Be the voice of support in leadership conversations with a clear view of service health, risks, and needs, make the case for tooling and headcount with data, and partner with Product and Engineering leaders so recurring issues get fixed for good.

- Run incidents & problems: Run major incident management (severity, war room, customer comms, RCA, post-incident review), set the RCA standard (clear root cause, fix, and prevention, written so a customer can read it), and use ticket and monitoring data to fix recurring issues at the source rather than patching the same thing every month.

- Hold the boundaries: Keep support focused on defects and queries, routing change requests through the CR process and larger work to Managed Services or Implementation, own the support-readiness gate for customers exiting hypercare, and agree internal turnaround commitments with Engineering, Product, and QA.

- Drive AI-first support: Own the roadmap for AI in support, taking it from first-pass analysis to AI resolving a real share of tickets end to end with engineers reviewing, build and improve AI agents for intake, classification, RCA, config fixes, QA, and customer updates (including MCP-based tools), turn customer knowledge into context agents can use, and coach the team to work with agents and grow into AI support engineers.

- Own tooling, data & customer comms: Get the team off spreadsheets and Slack onto proper support tooling, own the dashboards and alerts that flag an account going red before the customer does, set the standard for customer communication (progress first, current gap, next step, ETA), step in personally on strategic escalations, and work weekly with CSMs so service risks surface early, not at renewal.

 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (FIRST 90 DAYS)

- Set the direction: Learn the team, accounts, and data, then set the support org design and a 12-month plan covering structure, regional coverage, hiring, and the AI roadmap.

- Take over operations: Own daily operations - queue and backlog, workload balancing, standups, POC coverage per customer, and genuinely monitored intake channels - and keep the backlog

title: Alternative Investments Representative (OWN)
description:
About StartEngine

StartEngine is the FinTech powerhouse driving the future of fundraising and alternative investing. StartEngine was founded by Howard Marks, the co-founder of Activision (now valued at over $75B), with the goal of helping entrepreneurs achieve their dreams by removing funding barriers. Howard partnered with co-founder Ron Miller, a veteran entrepreneur and early advocate of equity crowdfunding, to build a platform that democratizes access to capital. In 2020, StartEngine welcomed Shark Tank judge and serial entrepreneur Kevin O’Leary (aka Mr. Wonderful) as Strategic Advisor and Investor. Since its inception, StartEngine has helped over 550 companies raise more than $ from retail investors, with investments starting at as little as $100.
Why merely back a company when you can own a piece of it?
Are you a licensed financial professional with your Series 7 and 63 registrations, ready to bring your talents to the fast-paced world of startup investing? StartEngine , the leader in equity crowdfunding, is looking for dynamic individuals to join our newest sales team. In this role, you’ll engage directly with our growing base of investors-building relationships, guiding them through investment opportunities, and helping them participate in the next wave of innovative companies. You’ll play a pivotal role in not only supporting investments into companies on our platform, but also in helping people invest in StartEngine itself. If you’re excited by startups, energized by meaningful conversations, and driven to help people grow their portfolios, this is your chance to be part of something transformative.
What you'll do

• Be a trusted partner to elite investors

• Build meaningful relationships with accredited investors across the U.S.

• Consult with investors to understand their portfolio goals and risk appetites.

• Serve as the inside connection for our exclusive gold level issuers.

• Identify opportunities to align investor interests with upcoming private offerings.

• Collaborate with internal teams to ensure a seamless experience from first call to closed deal.

• To put it simply = Drive deal flow and overall market momentum

What We're Looking For

• FINRA Registration required = Series 7, Series 63.

• Live and work in the United States.

• A natural relationship builder who thrives on meaningful conversations.

• Experience in outbound sales.

• A passion for finance, private equity, and cutting-edge technology sectors.

• Confidence in presenting investment opportunities with clarity.

• High emotional intelligence with the ability to navigate sophisticated client relationships.

• A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset - you’re not just a salesperson; you’re a trusted advisor.

Perks & Benefts

• 100% covered Medical/Dental/Vision - pick your own plan

• Generous Equity package

• Unlimited PTO and sick days

• Paid WeWork Usage (optional)

• 100% Remote

• Team Off-sites and Celebration Dinners

• Paid Maternity/Paternity leave

• 401K program

• Be part of one of the fastest growing parts of the FinTech Industry

• A chance to work with a highly profitable and rapidly expanding startup (not VC funded)

Roles and Responsibilities:
Role Summary : The Field Engineer I performs on time and accurate Preventative Maintenance in one or more modalities of equipment. The FE1 is aware of and follows all Field Modification Instructions and/or Instrument Service Information bulletins. Works with experienced Field Engineers, both onsite and remotely, to learn troubleshooting, repair and equipment installation techniques. Responsible for driving customer satisfaction through Service Excellence.

• Learn to complete on-time and accurate Preventative Maintenance, FMIs and/or ISIs.

• Work with experienced field engineers on basic troubleshooting and service repair needs on designated equipment.

• Effectively communicate and partner with teammates and colleagues.

• Effectively engage commercial counterparts, identify potential sales leads, participate in sales opportunities such as contract renewals, and assist with promoting and implementing revenue programs.

• Focus on customer needs and satisfaction, while building on and enhancing the relationship with the customer to ultimately become a perceived partner in their business.

Not because you just pulled together a report.

description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

Axon's mission is to Protect Life. For over 30 years we've made TASER energy weapons, transforming the policing landscape, but a TASER is more like an iPhone than a firearm: a complex piece of technology that agencies have to register, keep updated, and maintain, and how well they do that is critical to things going well in the field. Every minute we free agencies from maintaining their technology and tools is a minute they can spend on protecting the communities they serve.

Your impact

You'll own the Evidence.com experience agencies use to register, update, and maintain a fleet of hundreds of thousands of TASER devices. This isn't a new product. It's a ship that's already moving, with real customers who use it every week, and your job is to make it better. You'll start by understanding and instrumenting the system as it works today, then find ways to make demonstrable progress: less time, fewer errors, easier to use. Executives are engaged in several parts of this work, such as how device logs are presented, so what you improve gets seen.

About the team

Join our TASER software and data science team, a small and agile group within the TASER pillar at Axon. Everyone on it is technical. We move fast, build prototypes, and set high standards for our work and how we collaborate. We write requirements with AI, keep them in git, and review them through pull requests. Our work guides critical business decisions at the highest levels and becomes user-facing features in our products. We present to executives, to customers, and at major Axon events.

Location: This is a hybrid role, with an expectation of four days per week in either our Seattle or Scottsdale office.
Reports to: You'll report to Noah Burbank, Director of Software Product, TASER. Noah also runs TASER data science, is a former staff engineer, and has a PhD in Engineering from Stanford.

What you'll do

• Own how agencies set up TASER devices and docks: registration, onboarding, and upgrading.

• Own how device errors, logs, and new features are presented, so they tell customers something true and useful.

• Instrument the fielded experience, choose the metrics that matter, and show progress against them.

• Write requirements that engineers across hardware, firmware, and cloud can build from.

• Work across the broader Evidence.com ecosystem so changes there land well for TASER customers.

• Run field escalations down to a root cause, and fix the product so they don't come back.

What you bring

• 5+ years in a product management role. [Samantha: confirm for L8.]

• You've run a product already in market with a large customer base.

• Product experience tied to hardware.

• Connected devices experience. This one matters most.

• Ideally, a technical background: a degree in engineering or a hard science, or past work as a software or systems engineer.
